In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the Wnt-inhibitors Dkk-1 and sclerostin (SOST) in the pathophysiology of bone tumors and the development of novel therapeutic strategies to combat them.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Dkk- 1 is a potent inhibitor of osteoblastogenesis and bone formation, which in addition, enhances tumor cell stress resistance by transcriptionally activating aldehyde-dehydrogenease 1 through a non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway.
DKK-1 is a negative regulator of osteogenesis in osteosarcomas and is also a positive regulator of tumor cell survival and resistance to metabolic challenges.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Wnt-inhibiting protein Dkk-1 is not only involved in osteoblastogenesis but also in the survival of tumor cells through the activation of the ALDH1 gene.
we have shown that Dkk- 1 can have unexpected effects on tumor cells and that these are mediated through the activation of ALDH-1.

Dkk- 1, an inhibitor of the canonical Wnt-signaling pathway, is able to induce a non-canonical Wnt-signaling cascade in osteosarcomas, which results in the up-regulation of the aldehyde-dehydrogenease-1 (Aldh1), a stress response enzyme and marker for cancer stem cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Dkk- 1 is not only an osteolytic bone factor, but it can also have unexpected effects on tumor cells, such as increased stress resistance and ALDH1 expression.
Dkk- 1 has an unexpected role in promoting tumor cell survival and that this effect is mediated by a Wnt- signaling mechanism that is independent of the canonical Wnt pathway.
Dkk- 1 is not just an osteoclast activator, but also a survival factor for osteosarcoma cells.
